report.incidentSummary: At market open (03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST) on 2026-10-12, user stock order traffic through api-gateway rose to 437.3 req/s, exceeding upstream broker-api's 400 req/s rate limit on POST /orders. broker-connector immediately received HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). order-service retried failed orders, amplifying internal request rates to 915.6 req/s and saturating worker thread queues. This led to order latency doubling and approximately 15-20% of orders failing with HTTP 503 after retry limits were exhausted.
report.rootCauseStatement: Upstream broker-api enforced a strict 400 req/s rate limit quota on POST /orders. When market-open order placement reached 437.3 req/s at 03:45 UTC, broker-api responded with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. order-service retried rate-limited orders without effective global throttling or backoff, generating a 915.6 req/s retry storm that overwhelmed worker thread pools and caused order rejections after 2 retries.

hypotheses.cause: Market-open stock order traffic (437.3 req/s) breached upstream broker-api's 400 req/s rate limit on POST /orders, returning HTTP 429. Subsequent retries amplified order-service traffic to 915.6 req/s, exhausting worker thread pools and failing orders with HTTP 503.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct log and metric evidence from broker-connector shows HTTP 429 'limit 400 req/s' responses starting at 03:45:00.705Z. order-service logs confirm 231 instances of 'order rejected: broker rate limit after 2 retries' and worker thread pool queue overflow.

hypotheses.cause: order-service replica under-provisioning led to standalone CPU saturation and worker thread queue buildup directly at market open.
hypotheses.rationale: While past incident PIR-2008 had order-service capacity saturation, incoming gateway orders were only 437.3 req/s (normal 1.82x market open volume). The 7x jump to 915.6 req/s and worker queue buildup were caused by downstream rate-limiting retries rather than pure baseline under-provisioning.

hypotheses.cause: Database connection exhaustion or lock contention on order tables caused orders to fail and latency to spike at market open.
hypotheses.rationale: Database active connections remained flat (176.1 avg), lock wait time was nominal (~3.98 ms), slow queries were flat (2.9/min), order-service db_pool_wait_ms peaked at only 4.83 ms, and database CPU remained steady at ~37%.

facts.statement: At 03:45:00.705Z (09:15 IST), broker-connector began receiving HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('limit 400 req/s; retry-after 1s') from upstream broker-api on POST /orders (281 log entries between 03:45:00Z and 04:11:57Z).
broker-connector rate_limited_count metric on endpoint 'orders' surged from 0/min at 03:40 UTC to 631.2/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at 881.6/min at 04:00 UTC before subsiding to 0 by 04:15 UTC.
order-service logged 231 instances of 'order rejected: broker rate limit (429) after 2 retries' with HTTP status 503 between 03:45:40Z and 04:11:49Z.
At api-gateway, request_rate for route /v1/orders increased by ~1.82x from 240.7 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 437.3 req/s at 03:45 UTC, matching typical app-wide market-open increases across all routes.
order-service request_rate spiked from 129.2 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 915.6 req/s at 03:45 UTC (>7x jump), and error_rate spiked from 0.42% to 15.73% at 03:45 UTC, peaking at 19.52% at 03:50 UTC.
order-service latency_p95_ms increased from 320.6 ms at 03:40 UTC to a peak of 614.1 ms at 03:45 UTC, remaining elevated until 04:10 UTC.
order-service logged worker thread pool queue length above high watermark 18 times between 03:46:37Z and 04:06:08Z.
There were zero deployments or configuration changes for order-service, broker-connector, or database between 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z and 2026-10-12T05:15:00Z.

Database metrics showed no saturation: active_connections remained steady at 163-189, lock_wait_ms remained at 3.45-4.57 ms, slow queries remained under 8/min, order-service db_pool_wait_ms peaked at 4.83 ms, and database CPU stayed between 34% and 39%.

inferences.statement: The user request volume of 437.3 req/s at market open was normal user activity rather than an external DDoS or abnormal traffic surge, as all major gateway routes experienced a similar ~1.8x to 1.9x scaling.
The disparity between api-gateway /v1/orders incoming traffic (437.3 req/s) and order-service traffic (915.6 req/s) was caused by internal retries of orders rejected with HTTP 429 by broker-api.
High order-service CPU and thread pool queue saturation were downstream effects of holding and retrying rate-limited requests rather than standalone under-provisioning or database bottlenecks.

assumptions.statement: The upstream broker-api's 400 req/s rate limit is a fixed global quota that does not automatically accommodate temporary traffic bursts at Indian equity market open (09:15 IST).

timeline.event: Pre-market traffic baseline: gateway /v1/orders at 240.7 req/s, order-service error rate at 0.42%, broker-connector rate limits at 0/min.
NSE/BSE market open: api-gateway /v1/orders traffic surges to 437.3 req/s (~1.82x increase).
broker-connector receives first HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('limit 400 req/s; retry-after 1s') from upstream broker-api on POST /orders.
order-service begins rejecting orders with HTTP 503 after exhausting 2 retries; rate_limited_count reaches 631.2/min; order-service error rate jumps to 15.73% and request rate jumps to 915.6 req/s.
order-service worker thread pool queue length exceeds high watermark due to accumulated retrying threads; latency p95 peaks at 614.1 ms.
order-service error rate peaks at 19.52%; broker-connector rate limit errors continue at high volume.
broker-connector rate_limited_count on endpoint 'orders' reaches its maximum at 881.6/min; incident INC-5946 reported by On-call SRE.
Last HTTP 429 rate limit error received by broker-connector as market opening order burst subsides.
broker-connector rate_limited_count drops to 0/min; order-service error rate recovers to baseline 0.44% and latency p95 stabilizes at 372.6 ms.

confidence.rationale: The failure sequence is conclusively documented across metric and log telemetry: gateway ingress (437.3 req/s) exceeded the explicit 400 req/s upstream limit; broker-api returned explicit 429 errors stating the limit; order-service retries triggered a retry storm (915.6 req/s) and thread pool queue saturation, terminating in 503 rejections. Competing causes (database bottlenecks, gateway floods, code deployments) were conclusively ruled out.

gaps.description: Direct order-service CPU metrics and pod replica counts were not extracted due to tool budget limits.
gaps.impact: Minimal impact; order-service logs and request rate metrics conclusively explain high CPU as a symptom of the 7x retry storm rather than the root cause.

gaps.description: Contractual broker API quota documentation was not queried to confirm if 400 req/s is standard or customizable.
gaps.impact: Low impact on incident explanation, but relevant for sizing future rate limit increases with the broker.

recommendedActions.action: Implement a token-bucket rate limiter and request queue in broker-connector configured to cap outgoing POST /orders at 380 req/s, pacing requests rather than generating immediate 429s.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents upstream broker-api from rejecting bursts with 429 Too Many Requests and smooths traffic over market-open seconds.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate a 500 req/s order burst in staging and confirm broker-connector egress never exceeds 380 req/s and returns zero 429 status codes.

recommendedActions.action: Introduce exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaking on HTTP 429 responses in order-service instead of rapid unthrottled retries.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents retries from doubling order-service traffic from 437 req/s to 915 req/s and exhausting worker thread pools during rate limiting.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify that mocked 429 upstream responses back off according to the 'retry-after' header and thread pool queue depth remains below high watermark.

recommendedActions.action: Negotiate an increased market-open burst quota (e.g. 800 req/s between 09:14 and 09:30 IST) with the upstream brokerage partner.
recommendedActions.rationale: Baseline user demand at market open (437.3 req/s) organically exceeds the current 400 req/s contractual ceiling, which will recur as user numbers grow.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm broker SLA documentation and monitor rate_limited_count metric during next trading day market open.

report.justification: Although the investigation concluded without critic review, conclusive outcome is justified because timestamped logs from broker-connector and order-service explicitly record the upstream HTTP 429 'limit 400 req/s' responses and subsequent retry rejections, perfectly coinciding with gateway ingress metrics exceeding 400 req/s, while alternative hypotheses (database contention, code changes) were completely ruled out by negative metric and change log findings.

findings.summary: Database active connections, lock wait time, and slow queries did not spike at or before the 03:45 UTC market open. While order-service db_pool_in_use increased from ~13.6 to ~41.9 connections at 03:45 UTC, order-service db_pool_wait_ms only rose from ~2.8 ms to a negligible 4.83 ms peak, and database CPU remained flat (~37%). Database contention and connection starvation are ruled out.

observations.statement: Database active_connections remained steady around 163 to 189 connections (mean 176.1) throughout the window 03:15 to 05:15 UTC, with 172 connections at 03:44 UTC and 177 at 03:45 UTC, showing no spike.
Database db_lock_wait_ms remained nominal between 3.45 ms and 4.57 ms (mean 3.98 ms) throughout the window, showing 3.91 ms at 03:44 UTC and 3.91 ms at 03:45 UTC without any spike.
Database slow_queries_per_min remained low at 0 to 8 queries/min (mean 2.9/min) throughout the window, recording 4/min at 03:44 UTC and 4/min at 03:45 UTC.
order-service db_pool_wait_ms was between 2.1 ms and 2.8 ms prior to 03:45 UTC, slightly increased to 4.83 ms at 03:45 UTC, and averaged 3.01 ms across the window.
order-service db_pool_in_use rose from 13.63 at 03:44 UTC to 41.87 at 03:45 UTC, while database cpu_utilization remained flat between 34% and 39% (mean 36.93%).

Database contention and connection starvation are ruled out as root causes of order-service high CPU and errors: database lock waits, slow queries, and active connections were flat, and order-service connection pool wait times never exceeded 4.83 ms.

findings.summary: Api-gateway did not experience an abnormal spike in stock order request volume or error rates compared to normal market open levels. Route /v1/orders saw a typical ~1.82x increase at 09:15 IST (240.7 to 437.3 req/s), matching the uniform ~1.8x-1.9x market-open increase observed across all other gateway routes. Furthermore, gateway error rates for /v1/orders remained flat at ~0.3-0.45%. In contrast, order-service experienced a severe internal error rate surge (15-20%) and a 7x request surge (915.6 req/s) caused by downstream broker rate limiting and retry storms.

observations.statement: At api-gateway, request_rate for route /v1/orders increased from 240.7 req/s at 03:40 UTC to a peak of 437.3 req/s at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST market open), an increase of ~1.82x.

The ~1.82x traffic increase on /v1/orders at market open is consistent with the general app-wide traffic increase at market open, as other routes similarly scaled by ~1.8x to 1.9x (e.g. /v1/portfolio: 1.84x, /v1/assistant/chat: 1.82x, /v1/sip: 1.88x, /v1/auth/otp: 1.80x), indicating normal market-open user activity rather than an external request flood on stock orders.
At api-gateway, error_rate for /v1/orders remained near baseline levels (~0.30% to 0.45%), peaking at 0.45% at 03:50 UTC, showing no abnormal HTTP error rate spike at the gateway layer.

At order-service, request_rate spiked from 129.2 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 915.6 req/s at 03:45 UTC (>7x jump), and error_rate spiked from 0.42% at 03:40 UTC to 15.73% at 03:45 UTC and peaked at 19.52% at 03:50 UTC, remaining elevated above 18% until 04:05 UTC.

The discrepancy between api-gateway /v1/orders traffic (437.3 req/s) and order-service traffic (915.6 req/s) was driven by internal retries resulting from downstream broker rate limiting ('order rejected: broker rate limit after retries' logged 118 times in order-service).

findings.summary: No deployments, configuration changes, or pool sizing modifications were made to order-service, broker-connector, or database leading up to or during market open. Past incident PIR-2008 previously exhibited identical symptoms (order-service CPU saturation and timeouts at market open) due to inadequate replica pre-warming before the 09:15 IST rush.

observations.statement: There were zero deployments, configuration changes, or pool sizing changes for order-service, broker-connector, or database between 2026-10-11T21:15:00.000Z and 2026-10-12T05:15:00.000Z (and none dating back to 2026-10-09T00:00:00.000Z).

The only deployment or config change in the entire system during the window was CHG-48484 on mf-order-service at 2026-10-12T04:31:16.862Z, which is unrelated to stock orders and occurred well after market open.

Past incident PIR-2008 (2026-08-31 03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST) involved order-service CPU saturation (pinned at 100%) and timeouts at market open due to insufficient replicas before the open rush, resolved by raising the autoscaling floor before 09:00 IST.

The current incident was not triggered by any recent code deployment, configuration change, or pool adjustment on order-service, broker-connector, or database; rather, it matches historical capacity/saturation failure modes at market open or downstream broker rate-limiting.

recommendedActions.action: Implement a token-bucket rate limiter and request queue in broker-connector configured to cap outgoing POST /orders at 380 req/s, pacing requests rather than generating immediate 429s.

recommendedActions.verification: Simulate a 500 req/s order burst in staging and confirm broker-connector egress never exceeds 380 req/s and returns zero 429 status codes.

recommendedActions.action: Introduce exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaking on HTTP 429 responses in order-service instead of rapid unthrottled retries.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents retries from doubling order-service traffic from 437 req/s to 915 req/s and exhausting worker thread pools during rate limiting.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify that mocked 429 upstream responses back off according to the 'retry-after' header and thread pool queue depth remains below high watermark.

recommendedActions.action: Negotiate an increased market-open burst quota (e.g. 800 req/s between 09:14 and 09:30 IST) with the upstream brokerage partner.
recommendedActions.rationale: Baseline user demand at market open (437.3 req/s) organically exceeds the current 400 req/s contractual ceiling, which will recur as user numbers grow.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm broker SLA documentation and monitor rate_limited_count metric during next trading day market open.

# Investigation report: Stock orders failing at market open

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.85 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
At market open (03:45 UTC / 09:15 IST) on 2026-10-12, user stock order traffic through api-gateway rose to 437.3 req/s, exceeding upstream broker-api's 400 req/s rate limit on POST /orders. broker-connector immediately received HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). order-service retried failed orders, amplifying internal request rates to 915.6 req/s and saturating worker thread queues. This led to order latency doubling and approximately 15-20% of orders failing with HTTP 503 after retry limits were exhausted.

**Root cause:** Upstream broker-api enforced a strict 400 req/s rate limit quota on POST /orders. When market-open order placement reached 437.3 req/s at 03:45 UTC, broker-api responded with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. order-service retried rate-limited orders without effective global throttling or backoff, generating a 915.6 req/s retry storm that overwhelmed worker thread pools and caused order rejections after 2 retries.

## Hypotheses
1. **Market-open stock order traffic (437.3 req/s) breached upstream broker-api's 400 req/s rate limit on POST /orders, returning HTTP 429. Subsequent retries amplified order-service traffic to 915.6 req/s, exhausting worker thread pools and failing orders with HTTP 503.** — `broker-api`, rate_limiting_or_quota, confidence 0.85, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_7, ev_15, ev_16, ev_18, ev_19, ev_20, ev_21, ev_22, ev_23] · Contradicting: none
   - Direct log and metric evidence from broker-connector shows HTTP 429 'limit 400 req/s' responses starting at 03:45:00.705Z. order-service logs confirm 231 instances of 'order rejected: broker rate limit after 2 retries' and worker thread pool queue overflow.
2. **order-service replica under-provisioning led to standalone CPU saturation and worker thread queue buildup directly at market open.** — `order-service`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.12, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_10, ev_18] · Contradicting: [ev_7, ev_16, ev_19, ev_20, ev_21, ev_23]
   - While past incident PIR-2008 had order-service capacity saturation, incoming gateway orders were only 437.3 req/s (normal 1.82x market open volume). The 7x jump to 915.6 req/s and worker queue buildup were caused by downstream rate-limiting retries rather than pure baseline under-provisioning.
3. **Database connection exhaustion or lock contention on order tables caused orders to fail and latency to spike at market open.** — `database`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.03, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_14] · Contradicting: [ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_13]
   - Database active connections remained flat (176.1 avg), lock wait time was nominal (~3.98 ms), slow queries were flat (2.9/min), order-service db_pool_wait_ms peaked at only 4.83 ms, and database CPU remained steady at ~37%.

## Facts
- At 03:45:00.705Z (09:15 IST), broker-connector began receiving HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('limit 400 req/s; retry-after 1s') from upstream broker-api on POST /orders (281 log entries between 03:45:00Z and 04:11:57Z). [ev_19, ev_20, ev_21]
- broker-connector rate_limited_count metric on endpoint 'orders' surged from 0/min at 03:40 UTC to 631.2/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at 881.6/min at 04:00 UTC before subsiding to 0 by 04:15 UTC. [ev_23]
- order-service logged 231 instances of 'order rejected: broker rate limit (429) after 2 retries' with HTTP status 503 between 03:45:40Z and 04:11:49Z. [ev_19, ev_20]
- At api-gateway, request_rate for route /v1/orders increased by ~1.82x from 240.7 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 437.3 req/s at 03:45 UTC, matching typical app-wide market-open increases across all routes. [ev_7]
- order-service request_rate spiked from 129.2 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 915.6 req/s at 03:45 UTC (>7x jump), and error_rate spiked from 0.42% to 15.73% at 03:45 UTC, peaking at 19.52% at 03:50 UTC. [ev_15, ev_16]
- order-service latency_p95_ms increased from 320.6 ms at 03:40 UTC to a peak of 614.1 ms at 03:45 UTC, remaining elevated until 04:10 UTC. [ev_22]
- order-service logged worker thread pool queue length above high watermark 18 times between 03:46:37Z and 04:06:08Z. [ev_18, ev_19]
- There were zero deployments or configuration changes for order-service, broker-connector, or database between 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z and 2026-10-12T05:15:00Z. [ev_2, ev_8]
- Database metrics showed no saturation: active_connections remained steady at 163-189, lock_wait_ms remained at 3.45-4.57 ms, slow queries remained under 8/min, order-service db_pool_wait_ms peaked at 4.83 ms, and database CPU stayed between 34% and 39%. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_13]

## Inferences
- The user request volume of 437.3 req/s at market open was normal user activity rather than an external DDoS or abnormal traffic surge, as all major gateway routes experienced a similar ~1.8x to 1.9x scaling. [ev_7]
- The disparity between api-gateway /v1/orders incoming traffic (437.3 req/s) and order-service traffic (915.6 req/s) was caused by internal retries of orders rejected with HTTP 429 by broker-api. [ev_7, ev_16, ev_18, ev_19, ev_21]
- High order-service CPU and thread pool queue saturation were downstream effects of holding and retrying rate-limited requests rather than standalone under-provisioning or database bottlenecks. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_18, ev_19, ev_22]

## Assumptions
- The upstream broker-api's 400 req/s rate limit is a fixed global quota that does not automatically accommodate temporary traffic bursts at Indian equity market open (09:15 IST).

## Timeline
- **2026-10-12T03:40:00.000Z (09:10 IST)** Pre-market traffic baseline: gateway /v1/orders at 240.7 req/s, order-service error rate at 0.42%, broker-connector rate limits at 0/min. [ev_7, ev_15, ev_23]

## Confidence
0.85: The failure sequence is conclusively documented across metric and log telemetry: gateway ingress (437.3 req/s) exceeded the explicit 400 req/s upstream limit; broker-api returned explicit 429 errors stating the limit; order-service retries triggered a retry storm (915.6 req/s) and thread pool queue saturation, terminating in 503 rejections. Competing causes (database bottlenecks, gateway floods, code deployments) were conclusively ruled out.

## Gaps
- Direct order-service CPU metrics and pod replica counts were not extracted due to tool budget limits. (impact: Minimal impact; order-service logs and request rate metrics conclusively explain high CPU as a symptom of the 7x retry storm rather than the root cause.)
- Contractual broker API quota documentation was not queried to confirm if 400 req/s is standard or customizable. (impact: Low impact on incident explanation, but relevant for sizing future rate limit increases with the broker.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Implement a token-bucket rate limiter and request queue in broker-connector configured to cap outgoing POST /orders at 380 req/s, pacing requests rather than generating immediate 429s. [ev_19, ev_21, ev_23]
  - Why: Prevents upstream broker-api from rejecting bursts with 429 Too Many Requests and smooths traffic over market-open seconds.
  - Verify: Simulate a 500 req/s order burst in staging and confirm broker-connector egress never exceeds 380 req/s and returns zero 429 status codes.
- **[now]** Introduce exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaking on HTTP 429 responses in order-service instead of rapid unthrottled retries. [ev_16, ev_18, ev_21]
  - Why: Prevents retries from doubling order-service traffic from 437 req/s to 915 req/s and exhausting worker thread pools during rate limiting.
  - Verify: Verify that mocked 429 upstream responses back off according to the 'retry-after' header and thread pool queue depth remains below high watermark.
- **[next]** Negotiate an increased market-open burst quota (e.g. 800 req/s between 09:14 and 09:30 IST) with the upstream brokerage partner. [ev_7, ev_21, ev_23]
  - Why: Baseline user demand at market open (437.3 req/s) organically exceeds the current 400 req/s contractual ceiling, which will recur as user numbers grow.
  - Verify: Confirm broker SLA documentation and monitor rate_limited_count metric during next trading day market open.

## Justification
Although the investigation concluded without critic review, conclusive outcome is justified because timestamped logs from broker-connector and order-service explicitly record the upstream HTTP 429 'limit 400 req/s' responses and subsequent retry rejections, perfectly coinciding with gateway ingress metrics exceeding 400 req/s, while alternative hypotheses (database contention, code changes) were completely ruled out by negative metric and change log findings.
